label: third original token (t=2) in sequences starting with j
explanation: Fires at step t=2 (the third original input) whenever the first original token is j, so it marks a j two steps back at the very start of the sequence. A j two steps back at any other position does not trigger it. On dev, precision is 1.0 and it covers 99.9% of activation mass. Magnitude within the main mode is fairly uniform, roughly 0.6-0.83 of max, and depends somewhat on the second token (e.g. j l d gives 0.83, j n x gives about 0.59). Misses: about 1057 near-zero activations (about 0.01 of max) at t=1 in j-initial sequences, plus 12 rare copy-phase hits at t=5 in L=3 sequences of the form x j j <DEL> x j. These include the single highest activation (u j j: 1.0), but they carry negligible mass. Does not fire on the delimiter, and otherwise not in the copy phase.

issues: Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.940, F1 0.969, mass recall 0.9993, correlation 0.995. No false positives.

Missed activations are 1067 test steps holding 0.1% of mass. Almost all are at t=1 in j-initial sequences where the second token is w or d. The predicate (t==1)&(orig(0)==j)&(orig(1) in {w,d}) has precision 1.0 but activations near 0 (0.00-0.01 rel), so it is a systematic but negligible weak mode, not a real gap.

The copy-phase hits (L=3, pattern x j j <DEL> x j) are confirmed: test has one at 0.57 relative. The claim that these include the single highest activation was not confirmed on test, where the main-mode values are about 0.75-0.81. This is minor.
No firing at t=0, at the delimiter, or at t>=3 during the original phase. The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
